course_description: Introduction to Dental Disciplines B will continue to enhance students' emerging understanding of dental specialist disciplines prior to clinical practice the following semester. On completion, students will be able to take and interpret intra oral radiographs in a simulated environment and have an in-depth understanding of the laboratory and clinical processes that are involved in removable prosthodontic appliance fabrication. Students will also have developing interprofessional practice skills, including role clarification, team functioning and inter-professional communication towards achieving client centred care.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply knowledge of the anatomical structures of the orofacial region to the treatment of fully edentulous mouths.
Demonstrate knowledge of and familiarity with the laboratory skills and procedures required for practice of removable prosthodontics procedures.
Apply scientific principles of radiation and radiation safety to the process of taking intra-oral radiographs in a simulated environment.
Identify the radiographic features of structures of the orofacial region.
Develop interprofessional practice skills including role clarification, team functioning, interprofessional communication and client-centred care.

assessment_details.title: Interim Clinical Practice Performance (Pre-clinic/Peer Clinic)
assessment_details.category: Notebook/ Logbook, Performance, Practical/ Demonstration, Reflection
assessment_details.task_description: The purpose of this assessment is to evaluate the student’s pre-clinical/peer clinic performance at the interim stage and provide formative feedback to support improvement before the final clinical competence assessment at the end of semester. Course Coordinator in consultation with the pre-clinical/peer clinic supervisory team will complete a report based on student’s clinical performance during the assessment period and quality of critical self-reflections following each session. See Submission Guidelines for all components that must be submitted for the interim clinical practice performance task to be assessed. Detailed assessment criteria and rubrics will be provided on Blackboard. Two domains will be assessed to an expectations met (EM) or not met (ENM) standard and mapped to the Professional competency requirements for the accreditation body for this program - The Australian Dental Council (Professional Competencies of the newly Qualified Dentist) The domains being assessed are: 1. Professionalism, Communication and Health Promotion 2. Clinical Treatment and Evaluation To achieve a pass, the criteria are as follows: All domains are weighted equally, and the student must achieve a pass in each domain, and an overall pass. A pass in each domain will involve a student receiving 3 or fewer "expectations not met" (ENM) mark in Domain 1, and no more than 3 "expectation not met" (ENM) in Domains 2. An overall pass for the report will involve a student receiving 6 or fewer "expectations not met" (ENM) mark across the 2 domains. Please note: Written feedback will be provided for any areas to improve as this is formative. Students must reflect on feedback and demonstrate improvement in the latter half of the semester. Logbooks may be randomly audited by the Course Coordinator for authenticity and supervisor signatures. Any significant clinical concerns related to safety will be escalated immediately via course coordinator pathways and documented and taken into consideration for the assessment outcomes. There is no resubmission or resit available for this component. This is a formative assessment to enable the student to receive feedback on their developing clinical competency. Any significant clinical concerns pertaining to patient safety will be escalated via clinical communication pathways to the course coordinator and recorded on this report to be considered for the assessment outcome. assessment_details.title: IPCP Curriculum Assessment
assessment_details.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Essay/ Critique, Presentation
assessment_details.due_date: 28 September to 29 October 2026 (depends on group allocation; 2 weeks after last tutorial in each group)
assessment_details.task_description: Please refer to the assessment information on Learn.UQ for the assessment due date for your team. This is a team assessment, and all team members are expected to contribute equally to the team’s assessment items. Teams will be assigned during your first tutorial. There are three (3) parts to this assessment: Part One requires you to complete a worksheet and will draw on content from Module 1 of the IPCP curriculum focusing on role-clarification and negotiation, and relationship focused care and services. Length: There is no word limit for the worksheet. Part Two involves creating a 3-minute video which draws upon the content from Modules 2 and 3 of the IPCP curriculum focusing on team communication, team functioning and relationship focused care and services. Length: Video 3 minutes. Part Three involves a check-in with a tutor, to assess and reflect on processes of collaboration Length: approx. 10 minutes. Teams will need to submit Parts One and Two of your assessment in the Assessment tab on the HMBS1240 IPCP Learn.UQ course site. Additional information regarding submission will be provided on the HMBS1240 IPCP Learn.UQ course site. Please refer to the assessment information on Learn.UQ for further details and requirements for the assessment. Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Open assessment: In this assessment you can use resources such as your notes, course materials, and other tools, including AI, while completing the task. The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Submission: Online submission via Blackboard
The IPCP module is a Pass/Fail assessment task. Students who pass the module will receive a course grade based on the remaining assessment in the course.
For students who engage with the module, participate in the group work and submit a genuine attempt but do not achieve a pass grade for their submitted work, there will be given a second opportunity to pass the module by completing a reflective essay. If this task is successfully completed, a grade will be awarded based on the remaining assessment in the course. Students who do not engage with the module, fail to participate in the group work, or do not submit a genuine attempt, will be given an opportunity to complete a 5,000 word assignment on teamwork. Successful completion of this assignment will enable students to then pass the course with a maximum grade of 4 (if the remaining assessment in the course would result in a grade higher than 4, a maximum grade of 4 will be awarded). Students who fail the module who do not complete either the reflective essay or the teamwork assignment will be awarded a maximum grade of 3 (if the remaining assessment in the course would result in a grade higher than 3, a maximum grade of 3 will be awarded).
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.

learning_activities.topic: Preclinic Laboratory Students will learn the laboratory process of creating Full Dentures from initially constructing special trays on edentulous models to creating occlusal rims and setting teeth to partially waxing up a full denture.

learning_activities.topic: Clinical Lectures Clinical instructions on the treatment and management of the edentulous patient in order to create a set of functional, aesthetic removable dentures. Clincial coaching on radiographic anatomy and dental radiograph interpretation.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 10
learning_activities.topic: Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Modules Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Modules (Monday pm/ Thursday am) (Tutorials); Dates on Allocate + Participants will work in small teams in tutorial groups with students from Dentistry, Exercise Physiology and Sports Science, Midwifery, Nursing, Occupational Therapy, Pharmacy, Physiotherapy, Social Work and Speech Pathology. There are three modules that consist of on-line preparation and face-to-face learning activities. You will work in your team to engage in a range of learning activities to develop your knowledge and skills to help prepare you for working in teams when caring for clients. · In Module One, you will learn about relationship-focused care, role clarification and negotiation in the interprofessional context. You will explore trust and how to build trust and respect for colleagues and other health professionals, the person(s) receiving care, and their care team. · In Module Two you will develop the skills to communicate effectively with team members and appreciate the consequences when communication breaks down and is ineffective. This includes the role of communication in patient safety, handovers and transitions of care, health literacy, and communicating with diverse patient and population groups. · In Module Three, you explore team functioning, including barriers and enablers, consumer perspectives on team functioning in healthcare, and the psychosocial hazards which impact team functioning. You will also follow the healthcare journey of a client across the three modules. Learning outcomes: L05
